title: How few clicks make each of the five numbers?
description: A question from the book asks for the smallest number of clicks Systematic Sippy needs for each of five numbers. The video uses the biggest buttons first, writes each expression, adds the clicks, and checks that every expression adds back to its number.
teaching_notes: One idea: use the biggest buttons as many times as possible, so the clicks of each button are the digits of the number. Ask the class to add the parts of each expression before accepting it. Watch for students who skip a zero digit and press that button anyway.

video_script.why: The child has made 5072 and 8300 with the fewest presses by using the biggest buttons first.
video_script.substitution: Use the biggest buttons as many times as possible, and add the clicks of every button.
video_script.anchor: Find the fewest button clicks for each of five numbers, from 8300 to 367813, and write the expression
video_script.payoff_line: The fewest clicks are eleven, twenty one, twenty three, thirty and twenty eight

final_answer.spoken: the fewest clicks are eleven, twenty one, twenty three, thirty and twenty eight

video_script.design: One idea: biggest buttons first, so the clicks are the digits; add the clicks, then check by adding the parts. The method of the 5072 question is reused. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; Systematic Sippy with buttons +1 to +1,00,000; five numbers 8300, 40629, 56354, 66666 and 367813 in a column; a question mark sits in the anchor band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Systematic Sippy is a calculator with buttons from plus one up to plus one lakh. It wants to use as few clicks as possible.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>How few clicks make each of five numbers? They run from eight thousand three hundred up to three lakh sixty seven thousand eight hundred thirteen.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a row of buttons from +1,00,000 down to +1, the biggest button highlighted; a label biggest buttons first

marks.m1: the row of buttons appears with sizes shown
marks.m3: the label biggest buttons first appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A click of a bigger button adds more than a click of a smaller button.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>To use the fewest clicks, press the biggest buttons as many times as we can.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then we count the clicks of every button and add them.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, buttons from plus one up to plus one lakh, and the five numbers shown on the board.

beats.on_screen: To find: the fewest clicks for each number, and its expression

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the fewest clicks for each number, and write its expression.

marks.m1: 8300 is split into 8 thousands and 3 hundreds
marks.m3: 40629 is split into 4 ten thousands, 6 hundreds, 2 tens and 9 ones

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, take eight thousand three hundred. It is eight thousands and three hundreds, and nothing else.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Eight clicks and three clicks make eleven clicks.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Next, forty thousand six hundred twenty nine. It is four ten thousands, six hundreds, two tens and nine ones.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Four, six, two and nine clicks add to twenty one clicks. The thousands button is never pressed.

marks.m3: 66666 is split into six in every place

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, take fifty six thousand three hundred fifty four. It is five ten thousands, six thousands, three hundreds, five tens and four ones.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five, six, three, five and four clicks add to twenty three clicks.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Next, sixty six thousand six hundred sixty six. Every digit is six, so each of the five buttons is pressed six times.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Six clicks on each of five buttons make thirty clicks.

marks.m1: 367813 is read aloud on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, take three lakh sixty seven thousand eight hundred thirteen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It is three lakhs, six ten thousands, seven thousands, eight hundreds, one ten, and three ones.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The clicks are three, six, seven, eight, one and three, which add to twenty eight clicks.

marks.m1: the sum for 8300 and 40629 is written
marks.m2: the sums for 56354 and 66666 are written
marks.m3: the sum for 367813 is written and a tick appears beside each

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check each expression by adding its parts. Eight thousand and three hundred make eight thousand three hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Forty thousand, six hundred, twenty and nine make forty thousand six hundred twenty nine. The next two sums return their numbers too.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three lakh, sixty thousand, seven thousand, eight hundred, ten and three return the last number.

marks.m1: a tick sits beside every expression

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Each count adds the clicks of every button used.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The fewest clicks are eleven, twenty one, twenty three, thirty and twenty eight.
